body:
### Feature and its Use Cases

`send()` never retries: `request()` hard-codes `maxRetries = 0` for POST, even though the README says `retries` covers network errors/5xx and that identical sends are idempotent on Server 1.0+.

Add `retrySend?: boolean` to `ClientOptions` (default `false`). When enabled, `send()` uses the existing `retries` and backoff on 5xx and network/timeout errors only. 401, 413 and 429 still fail immediately.

Opt-in because pre-1.0 servers use random UUIDs, so a retry could create duplicates.

Useful for flaky mobile networks and proxies that return occasional 502/503.

### Additional Context

- Code: `RelayClient.request()` in `src/client.ts`
- Needs tests for retry on 503 and timeout, no retry on 401/413/429, and the default-off case
- Update the README `retries` row and the `send()` section
- No new dependencies

### Code of Conduct

- [x] I have joined the [Discord server](https://discord.gg/hjUhu33uAn) and will post updates there
- [x] I have searched existing issues to avoid duplicates
title: [FEATURE]: Opt-in retry for `send()`

body:
### Bug Description

In `RelayClient.request()` (`src/client.ts`), when a request completes with an HTTP 2xx status code but contains an invalid or non-JSON body (such as an HTML error page from a gateway/proxy, an empty body, or malformed JSON), `await response.json()` throws a `SyntaxError`.

This `SyntaxError` is caught by the general catch block, wrapped in `new RelayNetworkError(error.message)`, and retried across all retry attempts with exponential backoff.

This causes two issues:
1. Contract violation: Per `src/errors.ts`, `RelayNetworkError` is explicitly defined for errors where the network request failed and never completed. An unparseable HTTP 200 response completed over the network, so wrapping it in `RelayNetworkError` misinforms downstream error handlers that the client is offline.
2. Unnecessary retry latency: An unparseable response body will never become valid JSON on retry. The SDK repeatedly retries (default 3 retries), stalling the caller for ~7+ seconds with backoff delays before finally failing.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Point `RelayClient` to an endpoint that returns HTTP 200 OK with an HTML body (e.g., `<html><body>502 Bad Gateway</body></html>`).
2. Call `await client.receive('0xWalletAddress')`.
3. Observe that the client makes 3 sequential HTTP requests with exponential delays (1s, 2s, 4s).
4. Observe that the thrown exception is an instance of `RelayNetworkError` rather than a response parsing error.

### Logs and Screenshots

Integration test against local HTTP server:
[Client] Calling client.receive()... [Server] Received HTTP request # 1 /api/messages/0xTargetWallet [Server] Received HTTP request # 2 /api/messages/0xTargetWallet [Server] Received HTTP request # 3 /api/messages/0xTargetWallet [Client] Caught error after 4103 ms: Error Name: RelayNetworkError Error Message: Unexpected token '<', "<bod"... is not valid JSON Total HTTP requests received by server: 3


Suggested fix in `src/client.ts`:
```typescript
if (response.ok) {
  if (response.status === 204) return undefined as T;
  try {
    return (await response.json()) as T;
  } catch (err) {
    throw new RelayError(
      `Failed to parse response body as JSON: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`,
      response.status,
    );
  }
}

### Environment Details


### Box 4: Environment Details
```markdown
- Package: @aossie-org/thrubox-client
- Node.js version: 18+ / 20+ / 22+
- Browser: All modern browsers
- Branch: main

### Impact

Medium - Feature works but has issues

### Bug Description

In `RelayClient.request()` (`src/client.ts`), when a request completes with an HTTP 2xx status code but contains an invalid or non-JSON body (such as an HTML error page from a reverse proxy/gateway, an empty body, or truncated JSON), `await response.json()` throws a `SyntaxError`.

This `SyntaxError` is caught by the general catch block, wrapped in `new RelayNetworkError(error.message)`, and subjected to the exponential backoff retry loop.

This causes two issues:
1. Contract violation: `src/errors.ts` explicitly documents `RelayNetworkError` as representing situations where the request never completed and no HTTP response was received. Wrapping a completed HTTP 200 response in this error misleads downstream error handlers into treating it as a network outage.
2. Unnecessary retry latency: An unparseable response body will never become parseable on retry. Retrying forces the caller to wait through all backoff cycles (~7+ seconds on the default 3 retries) before the failure is reported.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Point RelayClient to an endpoint that returns HTTP 200 OK with an HTML body (e.g. `<html><body>502 Bad Gateway</body></html>`).
2. Call `await client.receive('0xWalletAddress')`.
3. Observe that the client makes 3 sequential HTTP requests with exponential delays (1s, 2s, 4s).
4. Observe that the thrown exception is an instance of RelayNetworkError rather than a response parsing error.

body: ### Bug Description When the relay responds `429 Too Many Requests` with a **negative numeric** `Retry-After` header (e.g. `Retry-After: -5`), the client stores it as-is. `RelayRateLimitError.retryAfter` becomes `-5` — an impossible wait duration. The HTTP-date path already clamps via `Math.max(0, ...)` (`src/client.ts:298`), but the numeric path (`src/client.ts:292-294`) does not. ### Steps to Reproduce ```js import { RelayClient } from "@aossie-org/thrubox-client"; const relay = new RelayClient("https://relay.example.org"); try { await relay.receive("0xWallet"); } catch (e) { // relay replies: 429 + "Retry-After: -5" console.log(e.retryAfter); // -5 ❌ (expected: 0) } 9989f16" /> ### Logs and Screenshots github.com/user-attachments/assets/ca955346-7820-4e39-bcfd-e697f ### Environment Details Package: @aossie-org/thrubox-client Version: 1.1.0 (published on npm — confirmed the published dist/index.cjs contains this code) Runtime: Node 18+, browsers ### Impact Critical - Application is unusable ### Code of Conduct - [x] I have joined the [Discord server](https://discord.gg/hjUhu33uAn) and will post updates there - [x] I have searched existing issues to avoid duplicates
title: bug(client): RelayRateLimitError.retryAfter is negative when server sends Retry-After: -5

body:
ThruBox Server is adding a per-mailbox sequence number (`seq`) to every message, plus `?after=<seq>&limit=<n>` on `GET /api/messages/{address}` (AOSSIE-Org/ThruBox-Server#69).

The SDK should expose this:

- `Message.seq`, optional because older servers don't send it. The `id` docs should stop promising a UUID, since IDs become content hashes.
- `receive(address, { after, limit })`.
- An opt-in cursor for `poll()`, so each poll fetches only new messages. The cursor should move forward only after the callback has handled the messages successfully, so a failed save is retried instead of skipped. Without the option, `poll()` should behave exactly as it does today, so existing apps such as Chainvoice are unaffected.
title: Support mailbox cursors (after/limit) in receive() and poll()

body:
### Problem

The README tells users to install `@aossie/thrubox-client`:

```bash
npm install @aossie/thrubox-client
```

That package is not published — `npm view @aossie/thrubox-client` returns a 404.
The published name is `@aossie-org/thrubox-client` (see `package.json`).

Every new user is blocked at the first step of the getting-started guide.

### Fix

Replace `@aossie/thrubox-client` with `@aossie-org/thrubox-client` in README.md.
Three occurrences: the install command, the Quick Start import, and the error
handling example.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All three occurrences updated
- [ ] `npm install @aossie-org/thrubox-client` copied from the README works in a clean directory
title: The README tells users to install `@aossie/thrubox-client`:
